disposition_reason: Laboratory water-treatment study reporting residual dissolved bismuth released from bismuth microspheres (10 to 20 µg/L) and its removal by clinoptilolite filtration (<0.3 µg/L).

study.method: ICP-AES (PerkinElmer Optima 8300) for bismuth in treated water; ion chromatography for bromate and bromide
lod: Bismuth reported as not detected below 0.3 µg/L after filtration (p. 4151)

material.label_as_printed: Residual bismuth in liquid phase after bromate reduction

findings.group: Reactor experiments across initial bromate 0.20 to 5.00 mg/L
findings.notes: Laboratory reactor water, not a drinking-water survey. Range as stated in text; supplement not reviewed.
findings.statistic_raw: kept at a low level of 10-20 µg/L

findings.group: Treated water after natural clinoptilolite filtration

unresolved: Per-condition residual bismuth values are in supplementary Tables S6 and S7, which were not part of the reviewed PDF.
non_numeric_findings: Authors state that bismuth released from treatment materials into drinking water should be regulated (p. 4151).
